questions.stem: Where do the sensitivity labels you apply to Fabric items come from?

options.text: Labels your organization publishes centrally for the whole tenant

questions.explanation: Fabric uses the sensitivity labels an organization publishes for its tenant.

questions.stem: At Harbor Health, a lakehouse carries the Confidential label. A semantic model and report are built on it. What can happen to their labels?

options.text: Labels never move from one item to another
Downstream inheritance can apply the label to items built from the labeled item

questions.explanation: With downstream inheritance, items created from a labeled item can receive its label, so protection follows the data.

questions.stem: A user exports data from a labeled Power BI report to Excel. What happens to the label?

options.text: The label is applied to the exported file, where the export format supports it
The label is shown as text in cell A1
The label is dropped on export

questions.explanation: Labels persist on supported exports such as Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, so the file stays protected outside Fabric.

questions.stem: Users can't see any sensitivity labels to apply in Fabric. What must be in place?

options.text: A Git connection on the workspace
Published sensitivity labels and the Fabric admin setting that lets users apply them

questions.explanation: Labels must be defined and published for the organization, and a Fabric admin must turn on the tenant setting that allows users to apply them.
